claim: Metformin delays aging or extends healthspan in non-diabetic older adults
gold_rationale: Documented consensus across geroscience leadership and FDA regulatory posture is that this is an untested hypothesis, not an established effect. The pivotal test — TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin), the first RCT explicitly designed to measure a composite multi-morbidity/aging outcome — was designed and received FDA conceptual acceptance but has NOT reported results (Justice 2018 DOI:10.1097/XCE.0000000000000159; Peng 2026 confirms it is 'currently underway', DOI:10.1097/JCMA.0000000000001374). The affirmative human evidence is observational and confounded: the widely-cited Bannister 2014 CPRD analysis (DOI:10.1111/dom.12354) showed metformin-treated DIABETICS outlived matched non-diabetics, but that is a diabetic population, a RETROSPECTIVE design vulnerable to immortal-time/prevalent-user and confounding-by-indication bias, and does not test non-diabetic older adults. The only completed RCT in non-diabetic older adults (MILES, NCT02432287) enrolled N=16 with a transcriptomic (gene-expression) primary endpoint — a molecular surrogate, not a clinical aging/healthspan outcome. Directly contradicting a healthspan benefit, a rigorous RCT (Konopka 2019, DOI:10.1111/acel.12880) found metformin BLUNTED exercise-induced gains in insulin sensitivity and VO2max in older adults. Net: no completed human RCT has demonstrated a clinical aging or healthspan benefit in non-diabetic older adults; the affirmative signal is observational/surrogate and partly contradicted. This is a textbook absence-of-evidence case → Insufficient.
outcome: Clinical aging / healthspan outcomes (delayed multi-morbidity, functional decline, frailty, mortality, or validated biological-age measures)

rows.citation: Metformin in Longevity Study (MILES). Albert Einstein College of Medicine. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02432287. Completed 2017.
rows.integrity_note: No retraction. Legitimate registered Phase 4 pilot RCT (verified COMPLETED on ClinicalTrials.gov, N=16, primary endpoint RNA-Seq transcriptome at 6 weeks). Very small pilot; primary endpoint is a molecular surrogate, not a clinical aging outcome.
rows.finding: Only completed RCT of metformin in non-diabetic older adults (age >60, impaired glucose tolerance). Primary endpoint was change in muscle/adipose gene-expression transcriptome via RNA-Seq at 6 weeks — a molecular surrogate of aging biology, NOT a clinical healthspan or aging outcome. Under-powered (N=16) and did not measure morbidity, function, or survival. Provides no clinical evidence for delayed aging.

rows.citation: Konopka AR et al. Metformin inhibits mitochondrial adaptations to aerobic exercise training in older adults. Aging Cell. 2019;18(1):e12880. DOI:10.1111/acel.12880
rows.integrity_note: No retraction (verified via PubMed; article type 'Randomized Controlled Trial'). Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, NIH-funded. Endpoints are physiological surrogates (insulin sensitivity, VO2max, mitochondrial respiration), not hard clinical aging outcomes.
rows.finding: In older adults (62 yr) randomized to metformin (n=27) vs placebo (n=26) during 12 weeks of aerobic exercise, metformin ATTENUATED the exercise-induced improvement in whole-body insulin sensitivity and VO2max and abrogated the gain in skeletal-muscle mitochondrial respiration. Directly contradicts a healthspan-promoting effect: metformin blunted a canonical healthspan intervention (exercise) in the target population.

rows.citation: Bannister CA et al. Can people with type 2 diabetes live longer than those without? A comparison of mortality in people initiated with metformin or sulphonylurea monotherapy and matched, non-diabetic controls. Diabetes Obes Metab. 2014;16(11):1165-73. DOI:10.1111/dom.12354
rows.integrity_note: No retraction. RETROSPECTIVE observational matched cohort (UK CPRD; PubMed article type 'Observational Study'). NOT prospective — schema enum lacks a 'retrospective cohort' bucket, so the nearest cohort category is used but temporality is retrospective. Vulnerable to confounding by indication, immortal-time/prevalent-user bias; hypothesis-generating only. Population is diabetic, not the claimed non-diabetic older adults.
rows.finding: Retrospective CPRD cohort: 78,241 metformin-monotherapy diabetics vs 90,463 matched non-diabetic controls (503,384 person-years). Metformin-treated diabetics had 15% LONGER adjusted median survival than matched non-diabetics (STR 0.85, 95% CI 0.81-0.90). The most-cited observational basis for a metformin longevity effect — but it is a diabetic population and retrospective/observational, so it cannot establish an aging/healthspan benefit in non-diabetic older adults (confounding by indication).

rows.citation: Justice JN, Niedernhofer L, Robbins PD, Aroda VR, Espeland MA, Kritchevsky SB, Kuchel GA, Barzilai N. Development of Clinical Trials to Extend Healthy Lifespan. Cardiovasc Endocrinol Metab. 2018;7(4):80-83. DOI:10.1097/XCE.0000000000000159
rows.integrity_note: No retraction. This is a CONSENSUS/DESIGN paper by the TAME leadership (PubMed article type 'Journal Article'), NOT a systematic review — the enum offers no 'narrative review'/'design paper' category. Not an outcomes trial. Establishes that the pivotal aging-outcomes RCT was still to be run.
rows.finding: Consensus design paper for TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin) — the first proposed RCT to test whether metformin delays a composite of age-related conditions in older adults. Documents that as of publication the trial was being designed to generate this evidence, i.e., the clinical aging-outcome evidence did not yet exist. Establishes the absence-of-evidence baseline. (Design/consensus paper, not a systematic review.)

rows.citation: Peng LN, Hsiao FY, Chen LK. Beyond disease treatment and prevention: from geroscience and molecular hallmarks to gerotherapeutics and precision geromedicine. J Chin Med Assoc. 2026;89(5):323-333. DOI:10.1097/JCMA.0000000000001374
rows.integrity_note: No retraction. NARRATIVE geroscience review (PubMed article type 'Review'), not a systematic review and not primary outcome data — enum lacks 'narrative review'. Used to confirm current status of the pivotal trial.
rows.finding: 2026 geroscience review confirms TAME — the first prospective trial designed to delay aging as a composite multi-disease outcome — is 'currently underway' and not yet reported. The strongest cited pharmacological evidence for metformin biological-age modification is a cynomolgus-monkey 40-month multiomics study (preclinical; ~6.41-year deceleration of proteomic biological age), NOT a human aging-outcome RCT. Confirms that no completed human RCT establishes delayed aging/healthspan in non-diabetic older adults.

baseline.text: A confident plain-LLM baseline would likely answer YES: 'Yes — metformin is widely studied as an anti-aging drug and observational data (e.g., the Bannister CPRD study showing metformin-treated diabetics outlived non-diabetic controls) plus strong preclinical lifespan-extension data support that metformin delays aging and extends healthspan; the TAME trial is testing exactly this.' This baseline conflates (a) preclinical and observational signals with confirmed clinical benefit, (b) a diabetic population with the claimed non-diabetic older adults, and (c) a DESIGNED trial (TAME) with a REPORTED positive one. It ignores that the only completed RCT in the target population (MILES, N=16) used a gene-expression surrogate and that a rigorous RCT (Konopka 2019) found metformin BLUNTED exercise benefits — so the correct verdict is Insufficient, not Supported.

provenance: Independently re-verified in this session. PubMed get_article_metadata on PMIDs 25041462, 30548390, 30906924, 41957871: all four resolve to the stated titles/DOIs/journals; none flagged 'Retracted Publication'. Bannister N (78,241/90,463), person-years (503,384), STR 0.85 (0.81-0.90) all match; PubMed article type 'Observational Study' (retrospective) — corpus 'prospective cohort' corrected in notes. Konopka confirmed 'Randomized Controlled Trial', n=27 metformin/n=26 placebo, attenuated insulin sensitivity+VO2max. Justice 2018 = consensus/design paper ('Journal Article'); Peng 2026 = 'Review' (narrative) — both mislabeled 'systematic review', corrected. ClinicalTrials.gov get_trial_details NCT02432287 (MILES): COMPLETED, Phase 4, N=16, primary endpoint RNA-Seq transcriptome at 6 weeks, age>60 IGT non-diabetic — confirms outcome_match=false, population_match=true. TAME not-yet-reported corroborated by Justice 2018 + Peng 2026.
notes: Key discriminators for the gate: outcome_match=false on MILES (surrogate transcriptome, not clinical aging) and population_match=false on Bannister (diabetic, not non-diabetic) are the two facts that collapse the affirmative case. The single directly-relevant RCT in the target population (Konopka) is CONTRADICTING (direction -1). No completed RCT measures the CLAIMED clinical aging/healthspan outcome in the CLAIMED population → Insufficient (absence of evidence), distinct from 'Not Supported'. FACT-CHECK CORRECTIONS: (1) Bannister design is RETROSPECTIVE observational, not prospective — the enum lacks a retrospective-cohort value so the field is left at the nearest cohort bucket with the temporality flagged in integrity_note. (2) Justice 2018 and Peng 2026 are a design/consensus paper and a narrative review respectively, not systematic reviews — enum lacks those categories, corrected in-text. None of these label fixes change direction, outcome_match, population_match, or the gold verdict.
